pages.text: Property articles by og | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content المنظمة العالمية للأرصاد الجوية (WMO) التقرير المؤقت عن حالة المناخ العالمي في 2023 أشارت المنظمة العالمية للأرصاد الجوية في أحدث نسخة من تقريرها المؤقت عن حالة المناخ العالمي إن عام 2023 حطَّم الأرقام القياسية المناخية بسبب ما شهده من ظواهر جوية متطرفة خلَّفت وراءها آثارًا من الدمار واليأس. الأطلس الدولي للسُحب يصف هذا الأطلس نظام تصنيف السحب وظواهر الأرصاد الجوية، كما يورد تصنيف الشهب الأخرى بخلاف السحب - الظواهر الجوية المائية، والظواهر الجوية اليابسة، والظواهر الجوية الضوئية، والظواهر الجوية الكهربائية. الكوارث المرتبطة بالطقس تزداد ذكر تقرير جديد شامل صادر عن المنظمة العالمية للأرصاد الجوية أن كارثة تتعلق بأخطار الطقس أو المناخ أو المياه حدثت يومياً في المتوسط على مدى السنوات الخمسين الماضية - مما أسفر عن مقتل 115 شخصاً وتسبب في خسائر يومية قيمتها 202 مليون دولار أمريكي. وزاد عدد الكوارث بمقدار خمسة أمثال على مدى فترة الخمسين عاما، مدفوعا بتغير المناخ، والطقس الأكثر تطرفاً، وتحسن الإبلاغ. ولكن بفضل تحسن الإنذارات المبكرة وإدارة الكوارث، انخفض عدد الوفيات بمقدار ثلاثة أمثال تقريبا. منظمة الأرصاد الجوية تعزز التزامها بالعلم انتخب الفريق العلمي التابع للمنظمة رئيساً جديدا لتعزيز تعاونه مع الأوساط العلمية ولدعم تطور ولايته في مجالات الطقس والمناخ والماء والعلوم البيئية والاجتماعية. إطلاق "التحالف من أجل تطوير الأرصاد الجوية الهيدرولوجية" اجتمعت اليوم اثنتا عشرة منظمة دولية تقدِّم المساعدة إلى البلدان النامية في مؤتمر الأمم المتحدة المعني بتغيّر المناخ لإطلاق التحالف من أجل تطوير الأرصاد الجوية الهيدرولوجية . وقد التزم أعضاء التحالف جماعةً بتكثيف الأنشطة الرامية إلى تعزيز قدرة البلدان النامية على توفير تنبؤات جوية

Property Management DOE is the fourth largest federal land manager, conducting its mission at 50 major sites on 2.4 million acres across the country. In addition to land, DOE’s assets include distinctive world-class facilities; irreplaceable natural and cultural history; and rare assemblages of plants, animals, and mineral resources. Numerous sites and tens of thousands of acres of land will be transferred to LM after active environmental remediation has been completed. LM will act as a steward for lands under its authority, overseeing the proper management of these man-made and natural resources and ensuring their beneficial use for current and future generations. LM considers environmentally sound future land uses for its properties, and directs a significant effort to maintaining healthy land and evaluating possible land reuse options. To accomplish this, LM implements DOE land use planning processes taking into account economic, ecological, social, and cultural factors surrounding each facility or parcel of land. Where compatible with DOE missions, LM will make excess lands and facilities available for government, public, and private use consistent with the tenets of sustainable and good land management practices. pages.title: Protecting the Grand Canyon's Silence and Beauty | National Geographic
pages.description: This photographer hiked the entirety of the Grand Canyon—a grueling trek done by only 30 people—and shares the trip's most lasting impact.
pages.text: Protecting the Grand Canyon's Silence and Beauty | National Geographic By Andrew Bisharat Photographs by Pete McBride Published October 24, 2018 • 9 min read Into the Grand Canyon Airs Thursday, February 21st @ 8/7c on National Geographic. Arguably America’s most recognizable landscape, the mile-deep Grand Canyon stretches as far as the eye can see. Though the canyon’s iconic panoramas and precipitous cliffs made for stunning images, when landscape photographer and filmmaker Pete McBride completed his winding 750-mile hike through the crown jewel of American public lands, it wasn’t the awesome vistas that left the most lasting impact. (Photos of p lateaus) One of his most profound takeaways was not what he saw but what he heard. A full moon rises over the canyon’s chief architect, the Colorado River, as the Nankoweep Granaries, roughly 900-year-old ancestral Puebloan storage caves, glow by headlamp. Photograph by Pete McBride “The silence,” McBride says. “The dense, crystalline silence that hangs over the place.” True wilderness. The silence was so absolute that the microphones on his camera had to be recalibrated. “There's this whole tapestry of wildlife sounds that you start to hear as time goes on,” says McBride, who completed his through-hike alongside writer Kevin Fedarko. The pair added their names to the short list of people—fewer than 30—who have undertaken the rugged journey. pages.text: Public Census Records Public Census Records Skip Navigation Within Public Census Records Public Census Records Who maintains copies of census records? The U.S. Census Bureau's National Processing Center (NPC) in Jeffersonville, Indiana, maintains copies of census records from 1910 through the most recent census, including those not yet publicly released under the 72-year rule. After the 72 years have passed, the Census Bureau transmits the records to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) who is responsible for making the records publicly available for viewing or purchase. When are census records made public? By law, records from the censuses of population and housing are made publicly accessible 72 years after each decennial census' "Census Day." The most recent publicly available census records are from the 1950 census, released April 2, 2022. The records from the 1960 Census of Population and Housing will be released in April 2032. How do I search for public census records? Visit the National Archives’ Census Records site to: Related Information Learn more about census records and what information they contain. Public Health Strategies for Antibiotic-resistant Neisseria meningitidis For Public Health Oct. 27, 2026 Key points CDC has detected penicillin- and ciprofloxacin-resistant serogroup Y meningococcal isolates in the United States. Using these antibiotics for invasive meningococcal disease in areas with resistance can lead to ineffective treatment and death. See CDC's updated guidance on treatment, prophylaxis, and surveillance for antibiotic-resistant invasive meningococcal disease. The problem Meningococcal disease is a rare but life-threatening illness requiring prompt antibiotic treatment for patients. Historically, resistance to the antibiotics used for meningococcal treatment and prophylaxis has been uncommon in the United States. The number of cases caused by penicillin- and ciprofloxacin-resistant Neisseria meningitidis strains has increased in recent years. In some parts of the United States, these cases account for over half of all reported meningococcal disease cases. The ACS PUMS files are a set of records from individual people or housing units, with disclosure protection enabled so that individuals or housing units cannot be identified. There is no requirement for publications resulting from work at the NCNR to have a NIST co-author, however you are encouraged to openly discuss this issue with the NCNR scientists responsible for the instrument you are using, and, where appropriate, include them as co-authors. Publications that have a NIST co-author must be approved by the Washington Editorial Review Board ( WERB ) . Your NIST co-authors will take responsibility for handling this process. Video Url The island of Puerto Rico is located approximately 1,000 miles (1,600 km) southeast of Miami, Florida, between the Dominican Republic in the Greater Antilles and the U.S. Virgin Islands. It is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the north and the Caribbean Sea to the south, and is home to more than 3 million people and more than 300 miles of beaches. Puerto Rico is in the primary path of Atlantic Ocean weather systems and experiences frequent hurricanes and tropical storms. The Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) vision for Puerto Rico is an electric system that aims to meet energy demands and power the island on a pathway to affordability, prosperity, national security, and energy dominance. To support Puerto Rico’s grid resiliency, we are prioritizing infrastructure delivery and bringing generation online. May 15, 2024 Español Put the Brakes on Diabetes Complications What to know People with diabetes are living longer with fewer complications. Greater awareness and better management of risk factors is helping. Find out what you can do to prevent or delay diabetes health problems. Diabetes complications are decreasing We've come a long way in reducing the impact of diabetes on people's lives. In the last 20 years, rates of several major complications have decreased among U.S. adults with diabetes. The greatest declines were for two leading causes of death: heart attack and stroke. This is real progress. People with diabetes are at higher risk for heart disease. They may also get it more severely and at a younger age than people who don't have diabetes. Diabetes complications are related Diabetes complications often share the same risk factors, and one complication can make other complications worse. For example, many people with diabetes also have high blood pressure, which in turn worsens eye and kidney diseases. pages.title: PWR: RFU wants to 'protect Red Roses' with reduction in international players - BBC Sport
pages.description: The RFU wants PWR to protect the interests of England's Red Roses, which could see a reduction in the number of international players in the league.
pages.text: PWR: RFU wants to 'protect Red Roses' with reduction in international players - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, (Left to right) Sophie de Goede, Hope Rogers, Ruby Tui and Olivia Apps are among PWR's foreign players By Sara Orchard , Rugby union commentator and Ceri Coleman-Phillips , BBC Sport Wales Published 3 hours ago World rugby has endured a few shocks and upsets in 2026 - and England's women losing back-to-back Test matches to Canada was among the biggest. But with 25 Canadians plying their trade on English soil in Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) last season, their success on the international stage comes at a time when PWR has been in discussions with the Rugby Football Union (RFU) to review the numbers of overseas players in the league. "We are keen to attract star talent into PWR to continue to make it the best league in the world," said RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney. "But we've also got to protect England Red Roses' interests as well." Changes have been planned for the 2027-28 PWR season around injury dispensation for foreign players, with the removal of club injury credit which helps to cover the cost of replacing an injured player. Only players who sustain an injury while on international duty for one of England's representative teams will be eligible. However, discussions have gone further around the numbers of English Qualified Players (EQP) required in matchday squads. Speaking to BBC Sport, Sweeney said: "We're talking about it. Indoor thermostats keep our homes comfy while outdoor thermometers tell us what to put on for the day. Our cars sense fuel and oil levels, engine temperature, the pressure our foot exerts on the accelerator and more. The trusty bathroom scale tells us our weight, while our smart phones, watches and rings flood us with data about our physical activity and health. These sensors generally operate according to the laws of classical physics, which describes the behavior of most everyday objects. For example, we can detect a change in a room’s temperature by monitoring the changing resistance of a wire or get our weight by measuring the compression of a scale’s spring or load cell. Most of today's sensors don’t use quantum mechanics, the strange, often counterintuitive rules that govern the universe at its smallest scales and coldest temperatures. But some scientists believe we’re at the dawn of an age of widespread quantum sensors: devices that use quantum properties to gain an advantage. These emerging technologies could open up a vast range of new applications in biomedicine and health

Emma Bond, currently Assistant Chief Constable at Police Scotland, was named in May as the preferred choice to replace Alex Franklin-Smith following his retirement in April. But more than four months later, the PCC announced that Bond's preferred candidate status had been withdrawn, meaning she will no longer take up the role. In a statement, Warwickshire PCC Philip Seccombe said no further comment would be made. Activity measurements for γ-ray-emitting radionuclides are made using 4πγ ionization chambers calibrated against primary standards developed in the Radioactivity Group. Primary standards of α- and β-emitting radionuclides are typically developed using 4πβ liquid scintillation spectrometry and 4πβ-γ anticoincidence counting. The calibration process also includes the identification and quantification of radionuclidic impurities by high-purity germanium γ-ray spectrometry. Recent development work has focused on therapeutic nuclides for nuclear medicine, radioimmunotherapy, bone palliation, and diagnostic imaging. The current focus of our work is on the development of standards and measurement tools for α-emitters used in Targeted Alpha Therapy and in the development of quantitative tools for preclinical imaging. pages.text: Rafael Nadal: Tennis legend set to join Real Madrid board of directors - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Rafael Nadal has made a number of appearances on the pitch at Real Madrid matches By Mike Peter BBC Sport Journalist Published 4 November 2026 Tennis great Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of Spanish football giants Real Madrid. Nadal won 22 Grand Slam titles, two Olympic gold medals and helped Spain claim five Davis Cups before retiring in 2024 . Real's members will be asked to approve the 40-year-old's appointment to the board at a meeting later this month. In a statement announcing the move , external , the club said Nadal was "one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world". "It is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our board of directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club," Real added. The tennis legend - a boyhood Real fan who holds member's number 67,778 - included a photo of himself as a child in a club kit in his response to the news. "I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board for proposing that I join the board of directors of Real Madrid," Nadal said in his post on X , external . "I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can." A commercial guidebook says: "The weather on Aniakchak is severe; life-threatening conditions can develop rapidly. Extremely violent winds in the caldera, particularly near 'The Gates,' can shred tents and prevent air rescue." A hefty budget and pre-tested skills and gear are absolutely necessary. Congress named the Aniakchak a national wild river in 1980. Its spectacular resources make rafting the Aniakchak a most rewarding experience. You can float from inside a volcano to the ocean, past spectacles of wildlife and geology. From Surprise Lake, the river flows a peaceful mile to The Gates.
